name: SLA Monitoring and Escalation
description: Periodically re-evaluates each open case's SLA status using business_process, escalates where the canonical rules say to, and keeps the Dynamics representation in sync.
trigger_detail: Recurring schedule (e.g. every 15 minutes), plus an event-driven re-check on case update

steps.name: Get current case state
steps.description: Retrieve current canonical case state via the connector boundary.

steps.name: Get SLA target
steps.description: Look up the case's response/resolution targets by category and priority.

steps.name: Evaluate SLA status
steps.description: Evaluate breach state against the target. This flow does not compute breach thresholds itself.

steps.name: Evaluate escalation eligibility
steps.description: Determine whether the case qualifies for escalation, and why, from its priority, stage, and SLA status.

steps.name: Branch on escalation reason
steps.description: Proceed to escalate only if a reason was returned; otherwise the run ends here for this case.

steps.name: Escalate case
steps.description: Move the case to ESCALATED, recording the reason business_process returned. Only reached when condition-escalate is true.

steps.name: Map to Dynamics representation
steps.description: Translate the escalated case, including current SLA fields, into a reference DynamicsIncident.

steps.name: Persist CRM representation
steps.description: Push the updated representation to the CRM boundary.

steps.name: Notify queue owner of escalation
steps.description: Notify the case's owning team that it has escalated.

steps.name: Record escalation audit evidence
steps.description: Record the escalation with its reason, case_id, and correlation_id.

idempotency_strategy: Re-running this flow for the same case_id before its stage changes must not create a duplicate escalation. business_process.lifecycle provides a canonical backstop: ESCALATED -> ESCALATED is not in ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS, so a repeat escalate_case call on an already-escalated case raises InvalidLifecycleTransitionError rather than escalating twice.
correlation_strategy: correlation_id = integrations.envelope.new_correlation_id(f'sla-monitor:{case_id}:{run_timestamp}'), unique per scheduled run so each escalation attempt is independently traceable.
failure_handling: If evaluate_sla or escalate_case raise for one case, that case's processing aborts, is recorded via an audit event with status=failed, and the scheduled run continues to the next case (partial failure isolation) rather than failing the entire batch.
